data.title: It was another great week for the average stock as market leadership shifts away from tech
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis and Isabel Wang

The S&P 500's tech sector just had its worst week in a year and a half, while an equal-weighted version of the index cemented a second-straight weekly advance

The average stock in the S&P 500 just had a decent week, although a slump in tech masked that shine at the index level.

Investors aren't bailing on the stock market, despite an ugly selloff in technology names this week that helped to saddle the S&P 500 with its worst weekly showing in months.

The S&P 500 SPX lost almost 2% even as the majority of the index's stocks actually advanced on the week. Seventy percent of stocks in the index posted weekly gains while 30% fell, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That helped the equal-weighted version of the index XX:SP500EW cement a second-straight week in the green. When the dust had settled, the S&P 500 had cemented its worst weekly showing since June, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Following a powerful but narrow tech-led rally, this week's action offered the latest indication that market leadership is shifting once again. While tech stocks and some industrial names tied to the artificial-intelligence build-out slumped this week, the average stock in the increasingly top-heavy S&P 500 made it through a difficult week largely unscathed.

Defensive and interest-rate-sensitive areas of the market moved sharply higher this week, as stocks that had lagged over the past two months shot upward. This has given hard-hit corners of the market a chance to shine.

"Given that there's growing concerns around the AI trade and volatility in spending these companies are doing, it just makes sense for investors to broaden their view a little bit and look for other opportunities," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial, in a phone interview Friday. "Now money is rotating out of tech into areas that had been really depressed."

Certainly, it helped that interest rates in the bond market saw a big pullback from recent highs, providing some broad relief to stocks.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, a popular exchange-traded fund that equally weights stocks in the index, rose 0.5% this week. By contrast, the S&P 500 saw its biggest weekly percentage drop since June 26.

The big drag on the S&P 500 is its largest sector, information technology XX:SP500.45, which was pummeled this week with a 6.4% drop. That left the tech sector with its biggest weekly loss since April 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Meanwhile, seven of the S&P 500's 11 sectors saw weekly gains, FactSet data showed.

"Nobody really wants to be out of the market," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, in a phone interview Friday. "If people were really genuinely concerned about the stock market right now, they'd be selling and not rushing to buy something else."

Among traditionally defensive areas of the stock market, the S&P 500's consumer-staples sector XX:SP500.30 surged 5% this week. Another defensive area, healthcare XX:SP500.35, had a big climb of 3.4%, while rate-sensitive stocks like materials XX:SP500.15 and utilities XX:SP500.55 also jumped sharply.

The decline in interest rates this week was significant, as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y "backed off pretty dramatically," Saglimbene noted. The 10-year Treasury rate fell this week to 5.097% on Friday, locking in its biggest weekly pullback since February, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Bond yields move inversely with bond prices.

That's down from the 10-year rate's recent high of 5.31% on Oct. 5. Yields on 10-year and 30-year BX:TMUBMUSD30Y Treasurys have risen to their highest levels in decades this year.

"With some improvement on the rates front, people do feel it's safe to move some money back into rate-sensitive sectors like financials XX:SP500.40, industrials XX:SP500.20 and real estate XX:SP500.60," Sosnick said.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury dropped Thursday despite a hot reading on wholesale inflation from the producer-price index that same day, partly because "there was a bit of a flight-to-safety trade on top of it surrounding CoreWeave," Sosnick said - referring to the neocloud company (CRWV) whose stock tumbled this week on worries over its AI-related borrowing.

Tech had been the stock market's "safety trade," rising when Treasury yields were spiking in September, as investors appeared confident about the AI trade continuing to power higher despite higher rates, said Keith Lerner, CIO at Truist Wealth, by phone on Friday.

Last month, tech looked like "the only place in town," he noted, "while all these other areas were beat up." Now, it appears the tide has turned.

"Instead of a broad-based selloff across the board, you're just seeing a rotation from tech to everything else," Lerner said. "A rotational market is better than when money is broadly leaving the market."

-Christine Idzelis -Isabel Wang

SHANGRAO, China, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. ("JinkoSolar" or the "Company") (NYSE: JKS), today unveiled Tiger Neo 5.0, an all-black residential solar module built on its all-new TAC technology. The first version to reach the market, an all-black 48-cell module, delivers a maximum power output of 510 W with a module efficiency of 25.52%. It was designed to redefine the upper limits of what a scenario-specific module can deliver in both appearance and efficiency for premium homes and other architecturally refined residences.

The module showcases a deeper, more uniform and more refined black appearance than conventional back-contact (BC) modules. Semiconductor-grade low- and high-temperature processes bring the power temperature coefficient down to -0.24%/℃, meaning stronger energy yield in high-temperature environments.

TAC technology combines the excellent carrier transport of TOPCon with the low-temperature processing and positive electrode passivation of HJT, pushing peak cell efficiency to 28%, approaching the theoretical limit of monocrystalline silicon cells. Together with a zero-gap cell layout and hidden-ribbon technology at module level, the module achieves an efficiency of 25.52%. Compared with conventional BC products, it delivers approximately 30 W more power, and a lower temperature coefficient. Its deeper, more premium black appearance blends seamlessly into residential rooftops— especially dark-colored ones — making it a standout in the residential module category for both power and aesthetics.

"Our vision for Tiger Neo 5.0 was to develop a panel tailored to premium residential rooftops. It pushes the boundaries of both performance and aesthetics with innovations in cell technology, passivation processes, structural design, module format and interconnections. With this launch, we aim to help move the industry toward solutions tailored to specific applications," said Charlie Cao, CEO of Jinko Solar Co., Ltd.

data.title: I'm 63 and diagnosed with lymphoma. Should I take my Social Security next year?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'My plan is to continue working as long as I'm able to do so and invest my Social Security benefits while I'm still earning a paycheck'

"It may remain stable, or it could progress, so for now, it's a wait-and-see situation." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I'd like your thoughts, please. I'll be turning 64 next January and have been thinking about starting my Social Security benefits then. I was diagnosed with lymphoma. It may remain stable, or it could progress, so for now, it's a wait-and-see situation. Am I overlooking anything or missing something important in considering this strategy? I'd appreciate any thoughts or advice.

My plan is to continue working as long as I can and invest my Social Security benefits while I'm still earning a paycheck. I understand there's a limit to how much you can earn before reaching full retirement age without affecting your benefits, and I believe I'd be earning around that limit.

When I'm 64

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I feel like a loser': My stock portfolio is swinging wildly. Is it finally time to worry?

Given the uncertainty surrounding your diagnosis, it's smart to regularly evaluate your financial security.

Dear (Almost) 64,

I'm sorry you're dealing with such a serious diagnosis on top of what is already a tricky decision. Your plans are realistic and optimistic, which is a good combination. If you are the lower-earning spouse, I see no problem with taking your Social Security in 2027. There is one caveat: if you claim at 64, applying for disability benefits later may not be an option if your lymphoma progresses. Before you decide, ask Social Security or a financial adviser how claiming early would affect that.

Otherwise, here's the trade-off: If you live well into your 80s, delaying benefits will result in higher lifetime monthly payments. Because a survivor's benefit is based on the deceased spouse's claiming age, a delay by the higher earner also means a larger benefit for the surviving spouse. If your health deteriorates, claiming earlier means you will enjoy your benefits now. Given the uncertainty surrounding your diagnosis, it's smart to regularly evaluate your financial security.

The earnings test is a big issue. Before full retirement age, Social Security withholds $1 in benefits for every $2 you earn above the annual limit ($24,480 in 2026). You say that you are currently earning "around that limit," and you also write that you make a good living. If you earn well above it, most or all of your benefits could be withheld, leaving no checks to invest. Social Security recalculates your benefits at retirement age so that money withheld is not lost.

You'll also have to account for any taxes on your investments. The Internal Revenue Service calculates tax due on your Social Security based on your "combined income," which consists of your adjusted gross income, tax-exempt interest, and half of your annual Social Security benefits. So up to 50% or as much as 85% of your Social Security benefits may be subject to federal income tax. Stacking benefits on top of a good salary makes that more likely.

If you live well into your 80s, delaying benefits will result in higher lifetime monthly payments.

When you reach full retirement age (67 for you, given your age), the Social Security earnings test no longer applies, so working won't reduce your monthly benefit. And while your Social Security benefits may be taxable on your federal return, some states do not tax Social Security benefits. So, given that you are still working and earning a good income, I understand your idea of investing your checks.

For married couples filing jointly, Social Security benefits typically aren't taxable at the federal level if your combined annual income is $32,000 or less. Between $32,000 and $44,000, up to 50% of benefits may be taxable; above $44,000, up to 85% may be taxable. These thresholds apply to combined income. See the IRS's Social Security benefits guidance and use Box 5 of your SSA-1099 when preparing your tax return.

If you keep working and collect Social Security, being taxed on your Social Security can sting, given that you are already paying 6.2% of your wages toward Social Security, in addition to the 6.2% that your employer contributes. That's because it goes toward a collective fund so Americans who can no longer work and/or wish to retire have a source of income. A tax adviser would be best able to run through all the scenarios.

Predicting the math

Your Social Security benefit at 64 would be reduced by 20% compared with your FRA. So let's assume that your benefit at age 64 is $2,000 a month; your FRA benefit at 67 would be close to $2,500 per month. Delaying from 67 to 70 increases the retirement benefit by 24%, before cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs). If your investments had a hypothetical 10% annual return before inflation, investing your checks might look attractive.

Let's take two scenarios: one with a 10% return and another with a more modest 7% return. If you invested your $2,000-a-month Social Security at 64, you could accumulate a lot in contributions, growing to roughly $80,000 at 7% or $83,500 at 10%, before taxes and fees. The exact total depends on the timing of your deposits, compounding, taxes and fees. The market rarely runs smoothly, and some years see a negative return, so nothing is guaranteed.

Obviously, waiting to collect your Social Security until 67 or later provides no accumulated investment, but your benefit would be higher by about $500 a month for life. Without investing, that extra $500 takes about 12 years to make up the $72,000 head start, so the break-even is roughly 79. If you claim at 64 and invest the benefits, the break-even point versus waiting until age 67 depends on your benefit, returns, capital-gains taxes, dividends, and how long you live.

Without investing, it would take about 12 years to make up the $72,000 head start.

A few reminders about the rules of survivor benefits: A surviving spouse who has reached FRA can generally receive up to 100% of their deceased spouse's benefit. You or your husband would not ordinarily receive both full retirement benefits added together. Instead, the survivor generally receives their own benefit or an eligible survivor benefit, with the applicable rules determining the amount payable. This is important if you are the higher earner.

Your diagnosis raises two other points. First, claiming reduced retirement benefits early could leave you worse off. If you can no longer work, you may qualify for Social Security Disability Insurance, which pays your full retirement age benefit without reductions that come from claiming early. (Some lymphomas are on Social Security's Compassionate Allowances list.) Second, Medicare begins at 65, with the Part B premium deducted from your Social Security.

Even taking your diagnosis into account, I wouldn't count out a long life just yet. The 10-year survival rates for lymphoma vary based on whether it is Hodgkin lymphoma or non-Hodgkin lymphoma, as well as the stage, your age, and the subtype. Survival statistics are very general and only give a glimpse into lymphoma mortality rates. Your oncology team is best placed to discuss your situation, assuming you want to factor that into your decision-making.

So what should you do? The fact that you're asking the question suggests that you're inclined to take your benefits earlier and keep working. Compare your actual Social Security estimates at 64, 67, and 70, and check how the earnings test will impact you for the years you plan to claim. If you are the higher-earning spouse, you may wish to wait. If your husband is the higher-earning spouse, he may wish to wait before claiming to maximize survivor benefits.

It's also not an apples-to-apples comparison. A delayed benefit provides you with a guaranteed income for life that is also adjusted for inflation. Investment returns are, as we know, uncertain.

data.title: Fed interest-rate decision this month is a closer call than markets think
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Here are some of the arguments against a Fed rate hike - and why some economists disagree with them

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks during a news conference last month after the Fed hiked interest rates for the first time in three years.

For weeks, investors and Federal Reserve watchers had been expecting the central bank to hold interest rates steady when it meets later this month. But fresh worries about inflation based on new data suggest officials aren't coming to the October meeting with a predetermined outcome.

Futures markets expect the Fed to hold rates steady in October, assigning only a 17% probability of an increase. But many economists think that the Fed meeting on Oct. 27-28 is a much closer call. Some see a good chance the Fed will raise rates.

"I think it's a 50-50 call," said Ethan Harris, former chief economist at BofA Securities, in an interview. Harris thinks the Fed should hike, but believes the committee has been "dovish" and may be reluctant to hike again so quickly.

The Fed hiked rates for the first time in three years in September, shifting away from a policy of slow rate cuts in 2024 and 2025 as inflation worries eased.

Fed officials characterized the increase at the time as part of a plan of limited hikes designed more to increase momentum in the process of bringing inflation down, rather than to combat a burst of inflation.

But September's inflation data, which came in higher than expected, changed the picture, and some economists think the Fed needs to move more quickly.

"I think October is a live meeting. We think the Fed will raise rates in October and December," said Matthew Martin, U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, in an interview with MarketWatch.

No preview from Warsh on what the Fed might do

Fed officials won't be speaking publicly until after the decision. In his last public comments before the Fed's blackout period, Chairman Kevin Warsh was neutral about monetary policy, saying he didn't like to prejudge meetings.

"I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year," Warsh said on the sidelines of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting in Bangkok.

The Fed seems to be facing two distinct scenarios.

One, laid out in an interview by former Philadelphia Fed President Patrick Harker, would be for the Fed to hike rates quickly by a quarter point in October and December, and then pause to assess the inflation outlook.

The Fed wants to get interest rates up to where they are putting downward pressure on the economy. Right now, rates in the current range of 3.75% to 4% don't seem to be accomplishing that, Harker said on CNBC.

Another benefit of swiftly raising rates would be to buffer the Fed's credibility as inflation fighters, he added.

Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics, wrote that he thinks the latest inflation data will prompt enough Fed policymakers to pivot to support the October and December option.

Martin, of Oxford Economics, said the September inflation data showed acceleration outside of energy prices, a worrying sign since goods outside of energy tend to be less volatile. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past 12 months, while the producer-price index showed wholesale inflation running at a 6.3% rate.

The second scenario for Fed officials would be to move more slowly in combating inflation by hiking only once every three months, with moves in December and March. This fits with the views expressed by many Fed officials who said before the latest inflation data that there was no urgency to hike.

Some economists think the Fed wants to hold rates steady in October because the central bank doesn't want to raise interest rates six days before the midterm elections on Nov. 3 and risk looking political.

Harris thinks the midterm concern is a small factor for the Fed. "There is no way to behave around the election that won't get criticism from somebody, and they will get pilloried by the president no matter what they do," he said.

Many economists said choosing between the two scenarios is a tough call for the central bank.

One benefit of a pause in October is that it will give the Fed more time to assess the data and determine how far to go, Aditya Bhave, head of U.S. economics research for BofA Global Research, wrote in a note to clients. The cost would be that the Fed risks falling behind the curve given the booming U.S. economy, he added.

Lindsey Piegza, chief economist for Stifel Financial, said an October hike would signal "an elevated level of concern" for inflation, creating an opening for the market to push rates higher and put more downward pressure on the economy. The more patient approach might make the public wonder if higher inflation is here to stay, she noted.

-Greg Robb

ASSA ABLOY sells PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners

PR Newswire

STOCKHOLM, Oct. 17, 2026

ASSA ABLOY has signed an agreement to sell HID's PKI business unit to Vista Equity Partners ("Vista").

STOCKHOLM, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PKI business unit (Public Key Infrastructure) provides digital trust, identity, authentication, encryption, and certificate management solutions. The business unit includes PKI SaaS - IdenTrust and HydrantID - credential management, and ZeroSSL.

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab) and RINVOQ® (upadacitinib) Data Highlight Long-Term Clinical and Endoscopic Outcomes Across Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) at UEGW 2026

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab) and RINVOQ® (upadacitinib) Data Highlight Long-Term Clinical and Endoscopic Outcomes Across Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) at UEGW 2026

PR Newswire

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 17, 2026
  • 20 scientific presentations underscore the breadth of AbbVie's leadership in Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) research programs
  • Latest long-term and real-world data with SKYRIZI®(risankizumab) and RINVOQ® (upadacitinib) provide additional insight into clinical and endoscopic outcomes over approximately three years in moderately to severely active Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis
  • New data evaluating endoscopic remission with investigational dual-targeting therapy ABBV-466 in patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease will also be presented

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced the presentation of 20 new scientific abstracts from its IBD portfolio at the 2026 United European Gastroenterology (UEG) Week, October 17-20 in Barcelona, Spain. Together, the data reflect the breadth of AbbVie's research across IBD, including established therapies studied over longer treatment periods and in real-world clinical practice.

"Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are chronic, lifelong conditions, and understanding how patients respond to treatment over time and in everyday clinical practice is critical," said Sofie Berg, Pharm.D., Ph.D., therapeutic area head, immunology, international medical affairs, AbbVie. "The data presented at UEGW 2026 build on our growing body of evidence that can help clinicians move toward favorable long-term outcomes for people living with IBD."

Key data to be presented include:

Long-term data in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC) and Crohn's disease (CD) – Open-label extension and post-hoc analyses add to the evidence base for clinical and endoscopic outcomes with risankizumab and upadacitinib

  • Risankizumab in UC: COMMAND showed sustained clinical and endoscopic outcomes up to three years of maintenance treatment. As-observed clinical remissiona rates of 54.0%–73.1% and endoscopic remissionb rates of 38.8%–53.5% were achieved at week 96 with 180mg across advanced therapy-naïve and advanced therapy-experienced patients.
  • Upadacitinib in CD: U-ENDURE as-observed analyses showed that clinical and endoscopic outcomes were maintained through approximately four years of treatment. At Week 144, clinical remissionc was achieved by 78.9% of patients receiving 15 mg and 86.6% receiving 30 mg. Endoscopic remissiond was achieved by 47.1% and 64.2% of patients, respectively.

Upadacitinib in the Real World: New Insights from Clinical Practice

  • Interim results from the real-world UPlift study showed that 70.2% of evaluable patients (N=497) with moderate to severe Crohn's disease achieved clinical responsee with upadacitinib within 12 weeks, with a median time to first response of 13 days.
  • A real-world claims analysis of patients (N=514) with UC or CD showed that patients who switched from a Tumor Necrosis Factor inhibitor (TNFi) to upadacitinib had lower rates of IBD-related hospitalizations (9.5% vs 16.3%) or surgery (6.9% vs 10.6%) over 12 months compared with patients who cycled to another TNFi.

Additional Findings on Risankizumab Subcutaneous Induction in CD

  • Data presented at UEGW will further expand on findings from the Phase 3 AFFIRM study evaluating subcutaneous risankizumab induction and maintenance in CD. Following the first presentation of AFFIRM results at the 2026 American College of Gastroenterology Annual Scientific Meeting, the UEGW presentations will provide additional analyses examining outcomes by prior advanced therapy exposure and further characterizing clinical and endoscopic outcomes among patients who responded to subcutaneous risankizumab induction and continued treatment.

aDefined as stool frequency (SF) score ≤ 1, and not greater than baseline, rectal bleeding score = 0, and endoscopic subscore ≤ 1 without evidence of friability.
bDefined as endoscopic subscore = 0.
cDefined as average daily very soft or liquid SF ≤2.8 and average daily abdominal pain (AP) score ≤1.0 and both not greater than induction baseline.
dDefined as Simplified Endoscopic Score for Patients with Crohn's Disease ≤ 4 and at least a 2-point reduction from baseline and no subscore > 1 in any individual variable, as scored by a central reviewer.
eDefined as the first day with ≥30% decrease in daily very soft or liquid SF and/or ≥30% decrease in daily AP score and both not worse than baseline AND a prospective 7-day average daily CR-PRO starting on the first day of daily CR-PRO; prospective 7-day average daily CR-PRO was defined as ≥30% decrease in average daily very soft or liquid SF and/or ≥30% decrease in average daily AP score and both not worse than baseline. Only patients with either baseline SF or AP >0 and both non-missing with at least one postbaseline assessment of CR-PRO2 are included.

SKYRIZI® (risankizumab) is part of a collaboration between Boehringer Ingelheim and AbbVie, with AbbVie leading development and commercialization globally. 

About SKYRIZI®
SKYRIZI is an interleukin (IL)-23 inhibitor that selectively blocks IL-23 by binding to its p19 subunit. IL-23, a cytokine involved in inflammatory processes, is thought to be linked to a number of chronic immune-mediated diseases.1 SKYRIZI is approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency for the treatment of moderately to severely active plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.1,2

On August 27, 2026, AbbVie announced submission of an application to the European Medicines Agency (EMA) seeking approval of SKYRIZI® for subcutaneous induction for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active CD.

EU Indications and Important Safety Information about SKYRIZI® (risankizumab)1 

Indications

Skyrizi (risankizumab) is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy.

Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in children and adolescents from the age of 6 years who are candidates for systemic therapy.

Skyrizi, alone or in combination with methotrexate (MTX), is indicated for the treatment of active psoriatic arthritis in adults who have had an inadequate response or who have been intolerant to one or more disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease who have had an inadequate response to, lost response to, or were intolerant to conventional therapy or a biologic therapy.

Skyrizi is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis who have had an inadequate response to, lost response to, or were intolerant to conventional therapy or a biologic therapy.

Important Safety Information

Risankizumab is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to the active substance or to any of the excipients, and in patients with clinically important active infections (e.g. active tuberculosis).

Risankizumab may increase the risk of infection. In patients with a chronic infection, a history of recurrent infection, or known risk factors for infection, risankizumab should be used with caution. Treatment with risankizumab should not be initiated in patients with any clinically important active infection until the infection resolves or is adequately treated.

Patients treated with risankizumab should be instructed to seek medical advice if signs or symptoms of clinically important chronic or acute infection occur. If a patient develops such an infection or is not responding to standard therapy for the infection, the patient should be closely monitored and risankizumab should not be administered until the infection resolves.

Prior to initiating treatment with risankizumab, patients should be evaluated for tuberculosis (TB) infection. Patients receiving risankizumab should be monitored for signs and symptoms of active TB. Anti-TB therapy should be considered prior to initiating risankizumab in patients with a past history of latent or active TB in whom an adequate course of treatment cannot be confirmed.

Prior to initiating therapy with risankizumab, completion of all appropriate immunizations should be considered according to current immunization guidelines. If a patient has received live vaccination (viral or bacterial), it is recommended to wait at least 4 weeks prior to starting treatment with risankizumab. Patients treated with risankizumab should not receive live vaccines during treatment and for at least 21 weeks after treatment.

Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported with use of risankizumab. If a serious hypersensitivity reaction occurs, administration of risankizumab should be discontinued immediately and appropriate therapy initiated.

The most frequently reported adverse reactions were upper respiratory infections (13% in psoriasis, 15.6% in Crohn's disease and 26.2% in ulcerative colitis).

Commonly (≥ 1/100 to < 1/10) reported adverse reactions included tinea infections, headache, pruritus, rash, eczema, fatigue, and injection site reactions.

This is not a complete summary of all safety information.

About RINVOQ® (upadacitinib)
Discovered and developed by AbbVie scientists, RINVOQ is a selective and reversible JAK inhibitor that is being studied in several immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.3,4 In human cellular assays, RINVOQ preferentially inhibits signaling by JAK1 or JAK1/3 with functional selectivity over cytokine receptors that signal via pairs of JAK2.3

Upadacitinib (RINVOQ) is being studied in Phase 3 clinical trials for hidradenitis suppurativa, Takayasu arteritis and systemic lupus erythematosus and in pediatric studies for systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis, atopic dermatitis, ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.

EU Indications and Important Safety Information about RINVOQ® (upadacitinib)3

Indications

Rheumatoid arthritis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in adult patients who have responded inadequately to, or who are intolerant to one or more disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs). RINVOQ may be used as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate.

Psoriatic arthritis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) in adult patients who have responded inadequately to, or who are intolerant to one or more DMARDs. RINVOQ may be used as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate.

Polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of active polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (pJIA) [polyarticular rheumatoid factor positive {RF+} or negative {RF-}, extended oligoarticular], in patients 2 years of age and older who have responded inadequately to, or who are intolerant to one or more DMARDs. RINVOQ may be used as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate.

Axial spondyloarthritis
Non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA) 
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis in adult patients with objective signs of inflammation as indicated by elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and/or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), who have responded inadequately to nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

Ankylosing spondylitis (AS, radiographic axial spondyloarthritis)
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of active ankylosing spondylitis in adult patients who have responded inadequately to conventional therapy.

Giant cell arteritis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of giant cell arteritis (GCA) in adult patients.

Atopic dermatitis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of moderate to severe atopic dermatitis (AD) in adults and adolescents 12 years and older who are candidates for systemic therapy.

Alopecia areata
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents 12 years and older.

Vitiligo
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of non-segmental vitiligo in adults and adolescents 12 years and older who are candidates for systemic therapy.

Ulcerative colitis
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (UC) who have had an inadequate response, lost response or were intolerant to either conventional therapy or a biologic agent.

Crohn's disease
RINVOQ is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease who have had an inadequate response, lost response or were intolerant to either conventional therapy or a biologic agent.

Important Safety Information

Contraindications
RINVOQ is contraindicated in patients hypersensitive to the active substance or to any of the excipients, in patients with active tuberculosis (TB) or active serious infections, in patients with severe hepatic impairment, and during pregnancy.

Special warnings and precautions for use
RINVOQ should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available in patients:

- 65 years of age and older;
- patients with history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular (CV) disease or other CV risk factors (such as current or past long-time smokers);
- patients with malignancy risk factors (e.g. current malignancy or history of malignancy).

Use in patients 65 years of age and older
Considering the increased risk of MACE, malignancies, serious infections, and all-cause mortality in patients ≥65 years of age, as observed in a large randomised study of tofacitinib (another Janus Kinase (JAK) inhibitor), RINVOQ should only be used in these patients if no suitable treatment alternatives are available. In patients ≥65 years of age, there is an increased risk of adverse reactions with RINVOQ 30 mg once daily. Consequently, the recommended dose for long-term use in this patient population is 15 mg once daily.

Immunosuppressive medicinal products
Use in combination with other potent immunosuppressants is not recommended.

Serious infections
Serious and sometimes fatal infections have been reported in patients receiving RINVOQ. The most frequent serious infections reported included pneumonia and cellulitis. Cases of bacterial meningitis and sepsis have been reported with RINVOQ. Among opportunistic infections, TB, multidermatomal herpes zoster, oral/esophageal candidiasis, and cryptococcosis have been reported. RINVOQ should not be initiated in patients with an active, serious infection, including localized infections. RINVOQ should be interrupted if a patient develops a serious or opportunistic infection until the infection is controlled. A higher rate of serious infections was observed with RINVOQ 30 mg compared to 15 mg. As there is a higher incidence of infections in the elderly and patients with diabetes in general, caution should be used when treating these populations. In patients ≥65 years of age, RINVOQ should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available.

Tuberculosis
Patients should be screened for TB before starting RINVOQ. RINVOQ should not be given to patients with active TB. Anti-TB therapy may be appropriate for select patients in consultation with a physician with expertise in the treatment of TB. Patients should be monitored for the development of signs and symptoms of TB.

Viral reactivation
Viral reactivation, including cases of herpes zoster, was reported in clinical studies. The risk of herpes zoster appears to be higher in Japanese patients treated with RINVOQ. Consider interruption of RINVOQ if the patient develops herpes zoster until the episode resolves. Screening for viral hepatitis and monitoring for reactivation should occur before and during therapy. If hepatitis B virus DNA is detected, a liver specialist should be consulted.

Vaccination
The use of live, attenuated vaccines during or immediately prior to therapy is not recommended. It is recommended that patients be brought up to date with all immunizations, including prophylactic zoster vaccinations, prior to initiating RINVOQ, in agreement with current immunization guidelines.

Malignancy
Lymphoma and other malignancies have been reported in patients receiving JAK inhibitors, including RINVOQ. In a large randomised active‑controlled study of tofacitinib (another JAK inhibitor) in RA patients ≥50 years of age with ≥1 additional CV risk factor, a higher rate of malignancies, particularly lung cancer, lymphoma, and non-melanoma skin cancer (NMSC), was observed with tofacitinib compared to tumour necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors. A higher rate of malignancies, including NMSC, was observed with RINVOQ 30 mg compared to 15 mg. Periodic skin examination is recommended for all patients, particularly those with risk factors for skin cancer. In patients ≥65 years of age, patients who are current or past long-time smokers, or patients with other malignancy risk factors (e.g., current malignancy or history of malignancy), RINVOQ should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available.

Hematological abnormalities
Treatment should not be initiated, or should be temporarily interrupted, in patients with hematological abnormalities observed during routine patient management.

Gastrointestinal perforations
Events of diverticulitis and gastrointestinal perforations have been reported in clinical trials and from post marketing sources. RINVOQ should be used with caution in patients who may be at risk for gastrointestinal perforation (e.g., patients with diverticular disease, a history of diverticulitis, or who are taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), corticosteroids, or opioids). Patients with active Crohn's disease are at increased risk for developing intestinal perforation. Patients presenting with new onset abdominal signs and symptoms should be evaluated promptly for early identification of diverticulitis or gastrointestinal perforation.

Major adverse cardiovascular events
MACE were observed in clinical studies of RINVOQ. In a large randomised active-controlled study of tofacitinib (another JAK inhibitor) in RA patients ≥50 years of age with ≥1 additional CV risk factor, a higher rate of MACE, defined as CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction and non-fatal stroke, was observed with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors. Therefore, in patients ≥65 years of age, patients who are current or past long-time smokers, and patients with history of atherosclerotic CV disease or other CV risk factors, RINVOQ should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available.

Lipids
RINVOQ treatment was associated with dose-dependent increases in lipid parameters, including total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol.

Hepatic transaminase elevations
Treatment with RINVOQ was associated with an increased incidence of liver enzyme elevation. Hepatic transaminases must be evaluated at baseline and thereafter according to routine patient management. If alanine transaminase (ALT) or aspartate transaminase (AST) increases are observed and drug-induced liver injury is suspected, RINVOQ should be interrupted until this diagnosis is excluded.

Venous thromboembolism
Events of deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) were observed in clinical trials for RINVOQ. In a large randomised active-controlled study of tofacitinib (another JAK inhibitor) in RA patients ≥50 years of age with ≥1 additional CV risk factor, a dose‑dependent higher rate of VTE including DVT and PE was observed with tofacitinib compared to TNF inhibitors. In patients with CV or malignancy risk factors, RINVOQ should only be used if no suitable treatment alternatives are available. In patients with known VTE risk factors other than CV or malignancy risk factors (e.g. previous VTE, patients undergoing major surgery, immobilisation, use of combined hormonal contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy, and inherited coagulation disorder), RINVOQ should be used with caution. Patients should be re-evaluated periodically to assess for changes in VTE risk. Promptly evaluate patients with signs and symptoms of VTE and discontinue RINVOQ in patients with suspected VTE.

Retinal vein occlusion
Retinal vein occlusion has been reported in patients treated with JAK inhibitors, including upadacitinib. Patients should be advised to promptly seek medical care in case they experience symptoms suggestive of retinal vein occlusion.

Hypersensitivity reactions
Serious hypersensitivity reactions such as anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported in patients receiving RINVOQ. If a clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction occurs, discontinue RINVOQ and institute appropriate therapy.

Hypoglycemia in patients treated for diabetes
There have been reports of hypoglycemia following initiation of JAK inhibitors, including RINVOQ, in patients receiving medication for diabetes. Dose adjustment of anti-diabetic medication may be necessary in the event that hypoglycemia occurs.

Medication residue in stool
Reports of medication residue in stool or ostomy output have occurred in patients taking RINVOQ tablets. Most reports described anatomic (e.g., ileostomy, colostomy, intestinal resection) or functional gastrointestinal conditions with shortened gastrointestinal transit times. Patients should be instructed to contact their healthcare professional if medication residue is observed repeatedly. Patients should be clinically monitored, and alternative treatment should be considered if there is an inadequate therapeutic response.

Giant cell arteritis
RINVOQ monotherapy should not be used for the treatment of acute relapses as efficacy in this setting has not been established. Corticosteroids should be given according to medical judgement and practice guidelines.

Excipients with known effect
RINVOQ 1 mg/ml oral solution contains 0.3 mg sodium benzoate in each ml.

Adverse reactions
The most commonly reported adverse reactions in RA, PsA, and axSpA clinical trials (≥2% of patients in at least one of the indications) with RINVOQ 15 mg were upper respiratory tract infections, blood creatine phosphokinase (CPK) increased, ALT increased, bronchitis, nausea, neutropenia, cough, AST increased, and hypercholesterolemia. Overall, the safety profile observed in patients with psoriatic arthritis or active axial spondyloarthritis treated with RINVOQ 15 mg was consistent with the safety profile observed in patients with RA.

The most commonly reported adverse reactions in AD trials (≥2% of patients) with RINVOQ 15 mg or 30 mg were upper respiratory tract infection, acne, herpes simplex, headache, blood CPK increased, cough, folliculitis, abdominal pain, nausea, neutropenia, pyrexia, and influenza. Dose dependent increased risks of infection and herpes zoster were observed with RINVOQ. The safety profile for RINVOQ 15 mg and 30 mg in adolescents was similar to that in adults. With long-term exposure, skin papilloma was reported in adolescents in the RINVOQ 15 mg and 30 mg groups.

The most commonly reported adverse reactions in the UC and CD trials (≥3% of patients) with RINVOQ 45 mg, 30 mg or 15 mg were upper respiratory tract infection, pyrexia, blood CPK increased, anemia, headache, acne, herpes zoster, neutropenia, rash, pneumonia, hypercholesterolemia, bronchitis, AST increased, fatigue, folliculitis, ALT increased, herpes simplex, and influenza. The overall safety profile observed in patients with UC was generally consistent with that observed in patients with RA. Overall, the safety profile observed in patients with CD treated with RINVOQ was consistent with the known safety profile for RINVOQ.

Overall, the safety profile observed in patients with GCA treated with RINVOQ 15 mg was generally consistent with the known safety profile for RINVOQ.

Overall, the safety profile observed in paediatric patients with pJIA treated with RINVOQ was consistent with the known safety profile of RINVOQ.

The safety profile of RINVOQ 15 mg and 30 mg observed in patients with alopecia areata was generally consistent with the known safety profile in patients with atopic dermatitis.

The safety profile of RINVOQ 15 mg observed in patients with vitiligo was generally consistent with the known safety profile in patients with atopic dermatitis. A higher incidence of hypercholesterolemia was observed in patients with vitiligo treated with RINVOQ 15 mg compared to placebo.

The most common serious adverse reactions were serious infections.

The safety profile of RINVOQ with long term treatment was generally similar to the safety profile during the placebo-controlled period across indications.

RINVOQ is available in 15 mg, 30 mg, and 45 mg prolonged-release tablets and 1 mg/ml oral solution. RINVOQ tablets and RINVOQ oral solution are not bioequivalent. Refer to the Summary of Product Characteristics for posology and method of administration.

World Winter Sports Expo 2026 Opens, Charting a New Decade for Ice and Snow and Outdoor Industries

World Winter Sports Expo 2026 Opens, Charting a New Decade for Ice and Snow and Outdoor Industries

PR Newswire

BEIJING, Oct. 16, 2026

BEIJING, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The grand event of the global ice and snow industry, the World Winter Sports Expo 2026 (WWSE 2026), was held in Beijing on October 15. As an important legacy of the Beijing 2022 Olympic Winter Games, this Expo aligns with China's "15th Five‑Year Plan" directives for the ice and snow industry. Its core mission is to expand the ice and snow economy, cultivate new productive forces in the sector, and promote deep integration of culture, sports, and tourism. It brought together representatives from government authorities, industry leaders, cultural‑tourism‑sports experts, outdoor film and media creators, and institutions across the entire value chain. Focusing on three strategic directions, upgrading the ice and snow industry, deepening culture‑sports‑tourism integration, and empowering the outdoor economy through technology, this WWSE features an opening ceremony, a main conference, multiple parallel sessions, and special thematic events. Together, these form a high‑end platform for achievement showcase, intellectual exchange, business matchmaking, and resource aggregation, aimed at driving higher‑quality growth for China's ice and snow and outdoor sectors.

Positioned at the pivotal starting point of a new decade of development, this Expo delivers a comprehensive upgrade: internationalization continues to reach new heights, the entire ice and snow value chain is presented in a coordinated way, scientific and technological innovation empowers the sector, ice and snow destinations pursue diversified growth, youth engagement in ice and snow sports advances through systematic promotion, forum agendas focus on niche tracks, the Ice and Snow Carnival offers a whole-scenario experience, industry-academia-research collaboration and industry services assume a stronger leading role, and a range of measures inject fresh vitality into the ice and snow economy.

At the Opening Ceremony of the WWSE 2026 and Global Ice and Snow Industry Summit, more than 200 domestic and international dignitaries gathered to witness the Expo's launch. Among them were: Yu Zaiqing, Honorary Member of the International Olympic Committee and Vice President of the Chinese Olympic Committee; Yue Li, Acting District Mayor of Shijingshan and Deputy Secretary of the CPC Shijingshan District Committee of Beijing Municipality; Tong Zhao, Deputy Secretary-General and Office Director of the Liaoning Provincial Organizing Committee of the 15th National Winter Games; Zhu Dongfang, President of Asia Data Group; Franz Roessler, Commercial Counsellor at the Austrian Embassy in Beijing, and Head of the ADVANTAGE AUSTRIA Beijing; Hong Ping, Vice President of Beijing Sport University; Wang Dong, Deputy Director of the Liaoning Provincial Bureau of Sports, and Full-Time Deputy Director of the Competition Department of the Liaoning Provincial Organizing Committee for the 15th National Winter Games; Gao Zhaoyi, Member of the Leading Party Members Group and Director of the Sports Bureau of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Zhan Wei, Vice Mayor of the Fushun Municipal People's Government of Liaoning Province; Zhang Li, Co-President of Asia Data Group; Li Jianrou, Olympic Short Track Speed Skating Champion; Wang Bingyu, World Curling Champion; Zhao Nannan, World Short Track Speed Skating Champion; and Jiang Yiyi, Deputy Secretary of the Party Committee and Dean, School of Leisure Sports and Tourism, Beijing Sport University.

Opening Ceremony Held in Grand Style, Uniting All Partners to Chart the Industry's Blueprint Together‌

On the morning of October 15, the Opening Ceremony of the WWSE 2026 and Global Ice and Snow Industry Summit was held. Closely following the development direction for the ice and snow industry set out in China's 15th Five-Year Plan, the Opening Ceremony took on the important missions of policy promotion, industry gathering, international dialogue and achievement release, and built a bridge for high-level dialogue among government agencies, international sports organizations, industry companies and research, cultural and tourism institutions. Serving both as a concentrated showcase of China's achievements in the ice and snow industry and as a key platform for the industry to assess trends, connect with resources and build consensus, it injected strong momentum into the innovative development of the ice and snow and outdoor industries throughout the year.

At the Opening Ceremony, Honorary Member of the International Olympic Committee and Vice President of the Chinese Olympic Committee, Yu Zaiqing, delivered the opening address. 11 years ago, he said, the Expo was launched alongside Beijing's successful bid to host the Olympic Winter Games. Today, it has grown into one of the world's leading platforms in the ice and snow industry. It has driven China's shift from being a major consumer market to becoming a powerful industry leader, and the Winter Olympics legacy continues to provide momentum. On this basis, he called for upholding the Olympic spirit of "Together", deepening international cooperation on ice and snow, and advancing the intelligent, green and international development of the industry.

Yue Li, Acting District Mayor of Shijingshan and Deputy Secretary of the CPC Shijingshan District Committee of Beijing Municipality, then delivered an address. The Expo has grown into an influential international ice and snow event and serves as an important link for Shijingshan to connect with global ice and snow resources. As a host district of the Beijing Olympic Winter Games, Shijingshan has continued to revitalize the Winter Olympic legacy, build a four-season events matrix, and promote the integrated development of ice and snow and the events economy. He expressed the hope to share the Winter Olympic legacy and jointly explore the blue ocean of the ice and snow industry with all parties, so as to help advance the global ice and snow economy.

As the representative of this year's Guest Province of Honor, Tong Zhao, Deputy Secretary-General and Office Director of the Liaoning Provincial Organizing Committee of the 15th National Winter Games, delivered an address at the Opening Ceremony. She noted that Liaoning has deep ties with WWSE, and this year it is drawing on its status as Guest Province of Honor to present the province's ice and snow resources, industrial achievements and cooperation opportunities. With the 15th National Winter Games set to be held in Liaoning in 2028, it is expected to become the first in China to have hosted both the National Games and the National Winter Games. Liaoning looks forward to learning from international experience through the Expo and extended a warm invitation to all parties to join it for the 15th National Winter Games.

Christophe Dubi, Olympic Games Executive Director of the International Olympic Committee, then delivered an address by video. He reviewed Beijing 2022's experience of hosting the Games across multiple competition zones and contrasted it with Milano Cortina 2026's approach of tailoring the Games to local conditions, proposing that the Games should adapt to the host rather than the host adapting to the venues. He also affirmed the value of forward-looking planning for Olympic venues and their post-Games reuse, and noted that climate change is confronting the industry with challenges ranging from snow resources to energy consumption, making the transformation of the ice and snow industry all the more urgent. He expressed the hope that those engaged in the industry would work together to explore a sustainable development path for ice and snow sports.

In the keynote speech session, Hong Ping, Vice President of Beijing Sport University, and Former Deputy Director of the Winter Sports Management Center, General Administration of Sport of China, shared his insights under the theme of "Reflections and Explorations on the High-Quality Development of the Ice and Snow Industry — Trend Transformation, Intelligent Manufacturing, and Safety Governance". He noted that China's sports market is huge in scale and that new indoor ice and snow formats are rising rapidly, with ice and snow consumption becoming an important lever for boosting domestic demand, yet the industry's development still falls short in several respects. He therefore called for a people-centered approach, building a coupled "human–machine–environment" mega-system and developing fifth-generation ski products that are science-based, smart, green, healthy and safe. This will drive the high-quality development of the ice and snow industry through demand pull and scientific and technological innovation.

In their addresses, Alexander Ospelt, President of International Ski and Snowboard Federation (FIS); Olle Dahlin, Honorary President of the International Biathlon Union (IBU); and Einars Fogelis, President of the International Luge Federation (FIL), conveyed a shared message from the global ice and snow industry: staying open and collaborative, and working together for the industry's development. They affirmed that the Expo has built a platform for global ice and snow exchange and cooperation, recognized the rapid growth of ice and snow sports in Asia, shared the outcomes of Milano Cortina 2026, and highlighted the importance of sustainable development in ice and snow sports. Looking ahead, they expressed the hope of using the Expo to deepen cross-regional and cross-generational exchanges and to jointly advance the continued prosperity of winter sports.

In the report release session, Co-President of Asia Data Group Zhang Li launched the "Report on China's Winter Sports Industry Development (2026)". Drawing on a comparison of global ice and snow industry trends, she pointed out that the scale of China's ice and snow industry had topped the one-trillion-yuan mark, the industry's growth had shifted from scale expansion to value enhancement, and that participation and the number of related enterprises were continuing to grow. The industry's spatial layout has moved beyond the old "strong in the north, weak in the south" pattern, and China's distinctive indoor ice and snow model is gradually being introduced to markets abroad. She also presented data and the current state of each segment, including ice and snow sports, equipment, tourism, culture and technology, while flagging the existing challenges in talent, technology, ecological protection and IP development. She proposed that the industry should focus on three main lines, the integration of multiple ice and snow business formats, digital and smart upgrading, and green, low-carbon and sustainable development, so as to keep advancing China's transition from a major ice and snow consumer market to a strong ice and snow industry power.

Following that, Jiang Yiyi, Deputy Secretary of the Party Committee and Dean, School of Leisure Sports and Tourism, Beijing Sport University, presented the report of "Innovative Practices of Huawei Smart Wearables in Skiing Scenarios". She noted that ski consumption is becoming more local and frequent, yet the industry still struggles with fragmented devices, data and services. Taking Huawei smart wearables as an example, she illustrated the value of technology in empowering the ice and snow industry. The devices can integrate data from skiing equipment and build an end-to-end safety assurance system for skiing by drawing on high-precision positioning, physiological sensing and multi-channel communication. They can also collect full-scenario skiing data, use AI-powered review to improve technique, and enable visualized data sharing that sparks ice and snow social interaction. She proposed that such digital technologies could improve ski profiles, optimize ski resort operations, and open up data across the industry chain. This would move the ice and snow industry from digital empowerment toward intelligence-driven development and convert cold resources into a hot economy.

The Opening Ceremony also featured the launch ceremony of the Ice and Snow Industry Investment and Development Platform. The platform was jointly initiated by Sunac China and BONSKI together with Victory Star Design, Eternal Star Ice & Snow, and Bin Jarallah Group. Focusing on the investment, construction and operation of indoor ice and snow venues in China, it will bring together resources spanning design, equipment and capital, resolve the difficulties and pain points in the construction and operation of indoor ice and snow venues, help China's ice and snow venues improve quality and expand capacity, and promote the high-quality popularization of ice and snow sports.

The "Ice and Snow Seeds in Thousands of Schools of Hundreds of Cities" — National Youth Ice and Snow Sports Promotion Public Welfare Program was also launched on site, with an opening ceremony in which an AIGC digital human exchanges a cross-spatiotemporal high-five with "Ice and Snow Teens". This innovative digital format broadens the reach of youth ice and snow education. Representatives of enterprises from the ice and snow industry platform, ski resort operations, ice and snow sports training and sports services sectors, together with representatives from the education sector, witnessed the official launch of the program. At the ceremony, Li Jianrou, Olympic Short Track Speed Skating Champion, Wang Bingyu, World Curling Champion, and Zhao Nannan, World Short Track Speed Skating Champion, issued an appeal to young people nationwide to be engaged in ice and snow sports, encouraging them to build strong bodies, temper their willpower and experience the unique spiritual power of winter sports. The program is jointly initiated by Asia Data Group and the Youth Ice and Snow Sports Education Committee of the Global Ice and Snow Industry Alliance. It will deliver ice and snow popularization courses and experiential activities in thousands of schools of hundreds of cities across China, further lowering the threshold for young people to participate in ice and snow sports.

The Opening Ceremony concluded with a round-table discussion themed "A New Ice and Snow Landscape Empowered by Science and Technology", moderated by Li Li, Deputy General Manager of Asia Data Group Beijing Branch. It brought together Franz Roessler, Commercial Counsellor at the Austrian Embassy in Beijing, and Head of the ADVANTAGE AUSTRIA Beijing; Li Jianrou, Olympic Short Track Speed Skating Champion; Florian Hajzeri, General Manager of TechnoAlpin Ice and Snow Equipment Zhangjiakou Co., Ltd.; and Yi Li, Vice President of BONSKI. The guests engaged in in-depth exchanges on topics including international cooperation in the ice and snow industry, technology-enabled ice and snow instruction, innovation in ice-making and snowmaking technology, and green operations of indoor ski resorts. Together, they explored a path for the industry's green, smart, and year-round sustainable development. They agreed that transforming and upgrading the ice and snow industry requires collaborative innovation across the entire industry chain, not just any single technological breakthrough. This innovation is necessary to make ice and snow sports greener, smarter, available year-round, and more inclusive.

Main Conference Convened for In-Depth Discussion, Empowering New Development with a Global Perspective‌

The Main Conference of the WWSE 2026 and Global Ice and Snow Industry Summit followed on the afternoon of October 15. Focusing on the industry's pain points and frontier directions, it brought together domestic local government representatives, university researchers and experts, and representatives of global ice and snow equipment companies. It provided industry insights from local practices, academic research, technological innovation, and overseas experience, offering a practical reference for the high-quality development of the ice and snow industry.

Zhang Li, Co-President of Asia Data Group, host of the WWSE 2026, was the first to address the Main Conference. In reviewing the Expo's ten-year journey, she noted that it has witnessed China's ice and snow industry's leapfrog growth over the past decade. The industry's scale surpassed one trillion yuan in 2025, and cold resources were successfully converted into a booming economy. The Expo has also seen the vision of engaging 300 million people in winter sports become a reality. It has continued to build a platform for industry matchmaking, promoting exchanges among governments and enterprises, between industry and finance, and between Chinese and international players, and helping to formulate industry standards. She proposed that scientific and technological innovation, consumption upgrading, and green and low-carbon development are the three major trends shaping the industry's future, and expressed the hope of deepening global collaboration through this platform to jointly advance the sustained development of the ice and snow industry in the world.

Dai Bin, President of China Tourism Academy (Data Center of the Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China), delivered a keynote speech titled "A Better Life on Ice and Snow". Ice and snow tourism has become an important part of people's pursuit of a better life. The industry's landscape has shifted from the "three-north snow arc", that is, a single east-west arc linking Northeast, Northwest and North China, toward three parallel development lines running from north to south. Two-way exchanges in ice and snow culture and tourism between China and the rest of the world continue to gain momentum. With policy and the market acting as twin drivers, the ice and snow industry chain keeps extending and digital technology is spawning new business formats. It is therefore all the more necessary to implement an ice and snow tourism doubling plan, step up efforts to build China into a strong ice and snow tourism nation, and advance the year-round sustainable development of ice and snow destinations.

Wang Dong, Deputy Director of the Liaoning Provincial Bureau of Sports, and Full-Time Deputy Director of the Competition Department of the Liaoning Provincial Organizing Committee for the 15th National Winter Games, delivered a speech with the theme of "Warm Winter Snow in Liaoning, Dual Events Spark New Momentum". The 15th National Winter Games will be held in Liaoning in 2028, making it the first province in China to host both the National Games and the National Winter Games. With four converging strengths, its event IP, ultra-low-energy venues, an equipment manufacturing base and warm winters with warm snow, Liaoning will focus its efforts on technology standards, green operations and the industrial market, open up the entire ice and snow industry chain and strive for sustained growth of the ice and snow industry. He also expressed the hope of working with all parties to establish a Liaoning landmark in the ice and snow economy.

Zheng Fang, Professor at Beijing Jiaotong University, and Chief Architect of the Beijing Jiaotong University Architectural Design & Research Institute, delivered a keynote speech titled "A Scientific Blueprint for Carbon Neutrality in Ice and Snow Venues". Drawing on a global skating rink database, he analyzed the status quo of energy consumption and carbon emissions at indoor skating rinks worldwide, noting that electricity is the main source of carbon emissions and that China's skating rinks hold notable potential for carbon reduction. He further proposed three core pathways to carbon neutrality for ice and snow venues, that is, expanding the use of green electricity, improving venue energy efficiency, and replacing refrigerants with environmentally friendly alternatives. Such measures, taken together, can substantially cut the industry's carbon emissions. He called on the entire industry to join forces in advancing the low-carbon and sustainable development of ice and snow venues.

From an international perspective, Vasiliy Afanasyev, Deputy General Director for International Projects at Rosa Khutor LLC., delivered a speech circling around "How Rosa Khutor Builds Customer Loyalty Through Operations in Winter and Summer". Drawing on its Winter Olympic venues, the resort has achieved year-round operation and built customer stickiness through well-groomed ski slopes, an unspoiled natural environment, rich activities and digital operations. To reach the Chinese market, the resort has opened accounts on WeChat and Xiaohongshu. It looks forward to deepening cooperation in ice and snow culture and tourism, as well as expanding two-way visitor flows, with the China-Russia mutual visa-free arrangement in place.

Michael Mayr, Sales Director of Italian TechnoAlpin Asia, delivered a keynote speech titled "Empowering the Ice and Snow Industry with Intelligent Manufacturing: TechnoAlpin's China Strategy and Global Vision". As a global leader in snowmaking and ice-making equipment that has served multiple Olympic Winter Games, TechnoAlpin has also built a deep presence in the Chinese market, with its equipment widely deployed at major ice and snow venues across the country. The company will set up a new base in Liaoning to provide snowmaking and ice-resurfacing equipment and technical support for several venues of the 15th National Winter Games, and looks forward to broader cooperation with industry partners.

Tertan Lorenzo, Head of Sales Export at Wintersteiger Sports GmbH, shared his insights under the theme of "How to Keep the Fun on the Slopes", focusing on how to cultivate the skiing community and retain ski enthusiasts. He likened the complete skiing experience to a jigsaw puzzle, in which infrastructure, ski lessons and ski equipment are all indispensable pieces. Only by getting every link right, and improving both the experience and the safety of skiing can ski resorts strengthen visitors' intention to return and keep expanding the skiing population.

Exhibition Displayed in Multiple Dimensions, Building a Trade Matchmaking Platform for the Ice and Snow Industry Chain‌

The exhibition segment of this Expo was held in Hall 2 of the Shougang Convention and Exhibition Center, with an exhibition area of nearly 15,000 square meters and eight specialized exhibition zones. Nearly 300 brands participated, and the exhibits spanned the entire ice and snow industry chain, from large-scale equipment upstream and venue solutions midstream to travel and tourism destinations and consumer equipment downstream, along with supporting services such as talent, IP and finance. Leading ice and snow nations from more than 20 countries and regions worldwide, including Austria, Italy, Norway, Russia, Japan, Slovenia and Canada, brought delegations to the exhibition, and internationally renowned brands such as TechnoAlpin, Doppelmayr, PRINOTH, FISCHER and Wintersteiger were featured in a concentrated display, setting a new high for its level of internationalization.

As the Guest Province of Honor this year, Liaoning set up three exhibition zones: Preparatory Achievements of the 15th National Winter Games, Liaoning Ice and Snow Industry's Cooperation and Exchange, and Liaoning Ice and Snow Tourism. Under the theme of "Charming 15th National Winter Games • Meet in Liaoning", these zones present the preparatory progress of the three competition zones in Shenyang, Dalian and Fushun, and showcase Liaoning's ski industry resources and opportunities for cooperation.

The National Pavilion Zone brought together advanced equipment, training systems and tourism resources from leading overseas ice and snow nations, creating a window for matching international ice and snow resources. The Austrian pavilion featured a number of well-known companies. For example, Axess presented smart ticketing systems and integrated access-control gate solutions; Sunkid exhibited family snow amusement facilities suitable for all ages; Wintersteiger rolled out professional race-grade ski waxing machines; PRINOTH showcased high-performance snow groomers; and Fischer brought a range of professional ski equipment. Taiga Motors from Canada unveiled its all-electric snowmobile as a highlight of the zone, offering green and smart mobility solutions for ski resort operations and polar research expeditions.

The Domestic Ice and Snow Economy Cluster Zone focused on segments including ice and snow destination operations, four-season culture and tourism development, smart ski resort operations and maintenance, and ice and snow IP development, presenting practices and innovative solutions from China's ice and snow industry. Changbai Mountain Wanda International Resort made a strong showing, sharing its proven experience in mountain ice and snow tourism development, year-round operations and visitor base cultivation. REXICE, a representative domestic ice resurfacer brand, exhibited its RX4020EV all-electric ice resurfacer, which has already been exported to overseas markets including Russia and Kazakhstan, demonstrating the global reach of Chinese-made ice and snow equipment.

The Winter Tourism Destinations Zone brought together sports, culture and tourism authorities from Beijing's Shijingshan District, Xinjiang and Liaoning to present ice and snow culture and tourism resources, investment promotion policies and year-round operating projects. With the theme of "Surprises in Shijingshan, Home of Major Events", the booth of Shijingshan District featured an ice-sculpture-style installation modeled on Big Air Shougang, a snowmaking experience zone and VR ski simulators. Italy's TechnoAlpin, under the theme of "Ice and Snow Equipment, Partners Joining Forces", focused on its TE10 snowmaker and ENGO ice resurfacer. The TE10 delivers powerful snowmaking even at extreme and marginal temperatures, while the ENGO ice resurfacer has served the Beijing 2022 Olympic Winter Games, vividly embodying an efficient and eco-friendly approach to ice products. Beijing Snowelan Sports Development, China general agent for Elan skis, SUFAG snowmakers, SPM safety nets and ALPINA and ROXA ski boots, appeared with ski equipment and on-site ski slope experience.

The Winter and Alpine Technology Zone presented large-scale snow machines including snowmakers, snow groomers, cableway and magic carpets, alongside indoor ice and snow construction technology, dry skiing and roller skating equipment, and a digital smart ski resort management and control platform. It showcases the latest advances in the localization and internationalization of ice and snow engineering and large-scale equipment.

The Ice and Snow Colleges and Industry Services Zone gathered domestic ice and snow colleges and industry service providers. They presented talent development systems, vocational skills training programs, event operations, and industry consulting services. This opened a channel between talent supply and industry development.

The Personal Winter Sports Equipment Zone brought together consumer-grade ice and snow gear such as smart ski goggles, carbon-fiber helmets, high-performance skis, ski protective equipment, and ski apparel, footwear and socks, with a number of new ice and snow products designed for Chinese teenagers and families making their debut.

The Outdoor Lifestyle Zone extended the reach of the ice and snow industry, displaying general outdoor products including recreational vehicles, camping gear, climbing and hiking equipment, and trendy sports apparel to promote the integrated development of the "ice and snow + outdoor" business format.

There was also a dedicated Robotics Application Zone within the exhibition area. Donghou Robotics and Yuto Intelligent Robotics presented a range of robotic products there, staging physical displays and offering immersive experience.

A number of product launches and debut events were held on site, drawing trade visitors of all kinds, such as buyers from home and abroad, sports, culture and tourism authorities from various localities, ski resort and resort operators, ski clubs, colleges and research institutions, and investment institutions. Parallel matchmaking sessions for ice and snow resources procurement and for scenic area resources, along with one-on-one B2B business negotiations, were also arranged to build targeted and efficient channels between supply and demand. Together they fully unlocked the Expo's platform value of promoting trade through exhibitions and advancing industry through conferences to open up the entire chain from product display and technical exchange to business negotiations and project implementation.

Diverse Side Events Staged Throughout the Expo, Creating a Platform for Industry-Public Exchange

Beyond the Opening Ceremony and the Main Conference, a number of important activities for the ice and snow industry were held. On the afternoon of October 15, the Annual Closed-Door Meeting of the Global Ice and Snow Industry Alliance took place as scheduled, at which member organizations reviewed the secretariat's work over the past year and held discussions on industry development for 2026, and the inauguration ceremony of the Ski Instructor Committee was held. The meeting also included in-depth internal discussions on issues of common concern to the industry, with a view to building an industry platform for industrial collaboration, self-regulation and the joint development of standards.

That evening, the Award Ceremony of the Aurora Award for International Winter Sports Leading Brands was held, honoring the year's outstanding brands and exemplary projects in the ice and snow industry. It set industry benchmarks, encouraged innovation among ice and snow companies, and steered the industry toward higher-quality development.

This Expo also set up a rich program of Ice and Snow Carnival activities, which served multiple purposes, including industry matchmaking, public outreach and cultural communication, opening up a channel between professional industry discussions and popular ice and snow participation.

On the morning of October 15, the "Meet the Champions" Salon met the audience on the public stage, where Olympic Short Track Speed Skating Champion Li Jianrou, World Short Track Speed Skating Champion Zhao Nannan, and World Curling Champion Wang Bingyu shared their competition experiences and reflections on ice and snow sports. This event brought the champions closer to ordinary spectators.

In the afternoon, the Promotion Conference of Famous International Ice and Snow Destinations was held, with leading international ice and snow destinations, British Columbia in Canada, Sochi in Russia and LAAX in Switzerland, taking the stage in turn to present their local ice and snow tourism resources and cooperation opportunities. Held in parallel was the IP Briefing themed as "Revitalizing Sports Venues: IP Empowerment for Sports Industry Operations", at which industry practitioners shared experience in sports venue IP development and commercial operations.

Meanwhile, the WWSE • Ice and Snow Carnival Stamp-Collection Tour was initiated to connect Winter Olympic legacy landmarks, winter sports venues, sports brand stores, and industrial-style dining spots. Visitors can collect stamps at each stop for a chance to win great prizes and experience the unique charm of Shougang Park, where industrial heritage meets winter sports.

A series of side events covered international cooperation, champion culture, venue IP, outdoor culture and tourism, startup incubation, and ice and snow films. These events complemented the Main Conference and parallel forums, bringing together professional industry discussions, commercial resource matchmaking, and public ice and snow outreach. This integrated approach fully unleashed the innovative vitality of the ice and snow industry.

Standing at the start of the 15th Five-Year Plan and a new decade, the World Winter Sports Expo 2026 will continue to unlock the Winter Olympics legacy and harness the collective strength of the global ice and snow industry. This will drive an upgrade to China's ice and snow economy, encourage deeper practical cooperation at home and abroad, and increase public access to ice and snow sports.

FLORIDA SOUTHERN COLLEGE HONORS DISTINGUISHED ALUMNUS LT. GEN. DONALD L. KERRICK WITH ROTC BUILDING DEDICATION AND STATEWIDE RAIDER COMPETITION

FLORIDA SOUTHERN COLLEGE HONORS DISTINGUISHED ALUMNUS LT. GEN. DONALD L. KERRICK WITH ROTC BUILDING DEDICATION AND STATEWIDE RAIDER COMPETITION

PR Newswire

LAKELAND, Fla., Oct. 16, 2026

LAKELAND, Fla., Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Florida Southern College honored distinguished alumnus Lt. Gen. Donald L. Kerrick on Friday, Oct. 16, with the dedication of the College's Army ROTC building in his name. The celebration continues Saturday, Oct. 17, with the second annual Lt. Gen. Donald L. Kerrick JROTC Raider Competition, welcoming 22 high school teams from across Florida to Florida Southern.

Through a generous gift, Kerrick is supporting significant renovations and equipment upgrades for Florida Southern's Army ROTC Moccasin Battalion. The investment will enhance training facilities and resources for future military officers and leaders. In recognition of his generosity and distinguished service, the facility will be named the Lt. Gen. Donald L. Kerrick Building.

"Lieutenant General Kerrick represents the very best of Florida Southern College and the extraordinary impact our graduates can have on the world," said Dr. Jeremy Martin, president of Florida Southern College. "From his distinguished service to our nation at the highest levels of military and civilian leadership to his continued investment in our students, his life exemplifies the values of leadership, character and service that define our institution."

A 1971 graduate of Florida Southern College, Kerrick was commissioned as a second lieutenant in the U.S. Army upon graduation. His distinguished military career included combat assignments in Southeast Asia and Operation Desert Storm, as well as senior leadership positions in military and national security operations. In 2000, he was appointed Deputy National Security Advisor to the President of the United States. He also served on the U.S. Balkans Peacekeeping Delegation, which helped negotiate the historic Dayton Peace Agreement ending the war in Bosnia.

Among his numerous military honors are the Defense Distinguished Service Medal, Legion of Merit and Bronze Star Medal. Florida Southern has also recognized Kerrick with its Distinguished Alumni Achievement and an honorary Doctor of Diplomacy degree.

The celebration continues Saturday as the College's Army ROTC Moccasin Battalion hosts the second annual Lt. Gen. Donald L. Kerrick JROTC Raider Competition. The event will bring together 22 high school teams to compete in five challenges testing physical endurance, discipline, leadership and teamwork, including a 5K run, One Rope Bridge, Cross Country Rescue, Tire Flip and Physical Team Test.

Teams will compete in male, female and mixed divisions, with awards recognizing individual challenges and overall performance. The annual competition also introduces high school cadets to the educational and leadership opportunities available through Florida Southern's Army ROTC program.

"Leadership is developed through experience, discipline and the willingness to push beyond perceived limits," said Lt. Col. Harry Dingle, professor of military science at Florida Southern College. "The Raider Competition gives young cadets an opportunity to put those principles into action. Lieutenant General Kerrick's remarkable career exemplifies that commitment to leadership and service, and his investment will help us continue developing future generations of leaders."

Established in 1951, Florida Southern's Army ROTC Moccasin Battalion has a longstanding tradition of preparing students for military service, with alumni including nine general officers and numerous distinguished military and civilian leaders.

The building dedication and statewide competition celebrate Kerrick's legacy of service while advancing the College's commitment to developing future leaders.
